correctness.rationale: The complement of Cr_n has two K_n cliques and only matching cross-edges. Its open-neighborhood complex decomposes exactly into P and Q, each the boundary of an (n-1)-simplex with n individually collapsible apex simplices, hence P,Q ~ S^(n-2). Their common faces are precisely the graph Cr_n (2n vertices, n(n-1) edges, cycle rank n^2-3n+1). For n>=4 these spheres are simply connected, so both inclusions from Cr_n are nullhomotopic, giving P union Q ~ S^(n-2) vee S^(n-2) vee (n^2-3n+1) S^2. Combinatorial Alexander duality on 2n vertices shifts cohomological degree k to dominance homological degree 2n-k-3; at n=4 the contributions coincide to rank seven. Independently enumerated all faces, P/Q identities, graph intersection, and binary boundary ranks for n=4,5: neighborhood Betti {2:7} and {2:11,3:2}; dominance {3:7} and {4:2,5:11}. Universal integral result comes from homotopy pushout and free graph cycles, not finite mod-two data.
